message.content:
<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Implement TimeTracking slice">
Implement the TimeTracking slice in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: CleanerCrm.TimeTracking context (TimeEntry, PayRate schemas + Earnings + PayrollExport modules + migration) and CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive with route.

FIRST: call mcp start_task with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", module_name="CleanerCrm.TimeTracking", then per child/surface (TimeEntry, PayRate, Earnings, PayrollExport, CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive). If module_name isn't accepted, resolve via list_requirements module_filter="TimeTracking"/"Timesheet".

Acceptance contracts (read ALL): test/spex/838_*/ (clock in/out on assigned job only — unassigned redirects with "not assigned" flash per reconciled criterion 7123; hourly = rate × hours; piece-rate fixed; running pay-period totals; owner CSV export at TimesheetLive ~p"/timesheets"; forgot-to-clock-out flagged, excluded from pay until owner resolves; export blocked while unresolved entries remain) and test/spex/844_*/ (cleaner-side earnings — the FieldLive surface doesn't exist yet; your context must expose per-job + pay-period earnings queries and drive-time policy visibility for it). Money: integer cents, Decimal math, "$X.XX" rendering. Honor the existing fixture contract: CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture calls CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id:, clocked_in_at:, clocked_out_at:}) — implement that exact function (clocked_out_at nil = open entry). Pay rates per cleaner (hourly or piece-rate basis), pay periods weekly.

Depends on CleanerCrm.Scheduling (stable, read-only: jobs + assignment) and Accounts/Users. Do NOT modify scheduling*, schedule_live/*, client_live/*, quoting*, notifications*, quality*, billing* (other agents own them).

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format, MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate, `mix spex test/spex/838_track_time_and_per-job_pay_in_one_system/` (criteria driving FieldLive clock buttons stay red; TimesheetLive-side ones should pass; report counts), `mix test` no regressions.

Final response: files, 838/844 pass counts, what stays blocked on FieldLive. Under 150 words.
</teammate-message>

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session

    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api

      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property

      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new

      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.MixProject do
  use Mix.Project

  def project do
    [
      app: :cleaner_crm,
      version: "0.1.0",
      elixir: "~> 1.19",
      elixirc_paths: elixirc_paths(Mix.env()),
      start_permanent: Mix.env() == :prod,
      aliases: aliases(),
      deps: deps(),
      compilers: compilers(Mix.env()),
      listeners: [Phoenix.CodeReloader]
    ]
  end

  # Configuration for the OTP application.
  #
  # Type `mix help compile.app` for more information.
  def application do
    [
      mod: {CleanerCrmWeb.Application, []},
      extra_applications: [:logger, :runtime_tools]
    ]
  end

  def cli do
    [
      preferred_envs: [precommit: :test, spex: :test]
    ]
  end

  defp compilers(:test),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :spex, :app]

  defp compilers(_),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :app]

  # Specifies which paths to compile per environment.
  defp elixirc_paths(:test), do: ["lib", "test/support"]
  defp elixirc_paths(_), do: ["lib"]

  # Specifies your project dependencies.
  #
  # Type `mix help deps` for examples and options.
  defp deps do
    [
      {:bcrypt_elixir, "~> 3.0"},
      {:phoenix, "~> 1.8.8"},
      {:phoenix_ecto, "~> 4.5"},
      {:ecto_sql, "~> 3.13"},
      {:postgrex, ">= 0.0.0"},
      {:phoenix_html, "~> 4.1"},
      {:phoenix_live_reload, "~> 1.2", only: :dev},
      {:phoenix_live_view, "~> 1.2.0"},
      {:lazy_html, ">= 0.1.0", only: :test},
      {:phoenix_live_dashboard, "~> 0.8.3"},
      {:esbuild, "~> 0.10", runtime: Mix.env() == :dev},
      {:tailwind, "~> 0.3", runtime: Mix.env() == :dev},
      {:heroicons,
       github: "tailwindlabs/heroicons",
       tag: "v2.2.0",
       sparse: "optimized",
       app: false,
       compile: false,
       depth: 1},
      {:swoosh, "~> 1.16"},
      {:req, "~> 0.5"},
      {:telemetry_metrics, "~> 1.0"},
      {:telemetry_poller, "~> 1.0"},
      {:gettext, "~> 1.0"},
      {:jason, "~> 1.2"},
      {:dns_cluster, "~> 0.2.0"},
      {:bandit, "~> 1.5"},
      {:assent, "~> 0.3"},
      {:cloak_ecto, "~> 1.3"},
      {:cloak, "~> 1.1"},
      {:credo, "~> 1.7", only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false},
      {:client_utils, "~> 0.1"},
      {:sobelow, "~> 0.13", only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false},
      {:sexy_spex, github: "JediLuke/spex", branch: "main"},
      {:boundary, "~> 0.10", runtime: false},
      {:code_my_spec_generators, "~> 0.1", only: :dev}
    ]
  end

  # Aliases are shortcuts or tasks specific to the current project.
  # For example, to install project dependencies and perform other setup tasks, run:
  #
  #     $ mix setup
  #
  # See the documentation for `Mix` for more info on aliases.
  defp aliases do
    [
      setup: ["deps.get", "ecto.setup", "assets.setup", "assets.build"],
      "ecto.setup": ["ecto.create", "ecto.migrate", "run priv/repo/seeds.exs"],
      "ecto.reset": ["ecto.drop", "ecto.setup"],
      test: ["ecto.create --quiet", "ecto.migrate --quiet", "test"],
      "assets.setup": ["tailwind.install --if-missing", "esbuild.install --if-missing"],
      "assets.build": ["compile", "tailwind cleaner_crm", "esbuild cleaner_crm"],
      "assets.deploy": [
        "tailwind cleaner_crm --minify",
        "esbuild cleaner_crm --minify",
        "phx.digest"
      ],
      precommit: ["compile --warnings-as-errors", "deps.unlock --unused", "format", "test"]
    ]
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Quality,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` context.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      %User{}
      |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Cleaner #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          email: "cleaner#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
        }),
        [:name, :email]
      )
      |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:email])
      |> Repo.insert()

    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)

    user
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      attrs
      |> Enum.into(%{
        property_id: property.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })
      |> then(&Scheduling.create_job(scope, &1))

    job
  end

  def recurring_plan_fixture(scope, property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} =
      attrs
      |> Enum.into(%{
        property_id: property.id,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        occurrence_count: 4
      })
      |> then(&Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, &1))

    plan
  end

  def availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, block} =
      attrs
      |> Enum.into(%{cleaner_id: cleaner.id, date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7), all_day: true})
      |> then(&Scheduling.create_availability_block(scope, &1))

    block
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7140Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7140 — Export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains

  The missing-clock-out state itself is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner forgets to clock out" spec. This spec's subject
  is how the payroll export reacts to that unresolved entry.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "payroll export is blocked while a time entry is unresolved" do
    scenario "export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner is assigned to a job", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "unresolved-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner clocked in on the job but never clocked out", context do
        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), context.cleaner)

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(cleaner_conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-in-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner attempts to export the pay period containing that job", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the export control is disabled with a message to resolve the open entry first",
            context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='export-csv-button'][disabled]"
               )

        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the unresolved job is called out for the owner to fix", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='unresolved-entry-job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story844.Criterion7129Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 844 — Clock in/out per job and see my earnings build
  Criterion 7129 — Cleaner cannot clock in to a job assigned to someone else

  Reconciled with story 838 criterion 7123: opening a job assigned to
  someone else redirects away entirely (the job page exposes entry codes,
  so unassigned cleaners must not see it at all). "Cannot clock in"
  follows from "cannot open".
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner cannot start time on a job assigned to someone else" do
    scenario "cleaner cannot clock in to a job assigned to someone else" do
      given_ "the owner has an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job at the Jones home is assigned to another cleaner, not me", context do
        other_cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "other-cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        me =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "me-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Jones"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: other_cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, me)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{me: me, job: job, conn: conn})}
      end

      when_ "I attempt to open that job", context do
        {:error, {:redirect, %{to: path, flash: flash}}} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{redirect_path: path, redirect_flash: flash})}
      end

      then_ "I am redirected away and cannot see the job at all", context do
        assert context.redirect_path == ~p"/field"
        assert context.redirect_flash["error"] =~ "not assigned"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I cannot start time on it", context do
        refute Map.has_key?(context, :job_live)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending ->
            {:error, :invalid_token}

          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt ->
            {:error, :expired_token}

          true ->
            {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
2	  use Ecto.Schema
3	  import Ecto.Changeset
4	
5	  schema "users" do
6	    field :email, :string
7	    field :name, :string
8	    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
9	    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
10	    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
11	    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true
12	
13	    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
14	  end
15	
16	  @doc """
17	  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.
18	
19	  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.
20	
21	  ## Options
22	
23	    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
24	      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
25	      Defaults to `true`.
26	  """
27	  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
28	    user
29	    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
30	    |> validate_email(opts)
31	  end
32	
33	  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
34	    changeset =
35	      changeset
36	      |> validate_required([:email])
37	      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
38	        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
39	      )
40	      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)
41	
42	    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
43	      changeset
44	      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
45	      |> unique_constraint(:email)
46	      |> validate_email_changed()
47	    else
48	      changeset
49	    end
50	  end
51	
52	  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
53	    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
54	      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
55	    else
56	      changeset
57	    end
58	  end
59	
60	  @doc """
61	  A user changeset for changing the password.
62	
63	  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
64	  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.
65	
66	  ## Options
67	
68	    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
69	      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
70	      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
71	      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
72	      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
73	      Defaults to `true`.
74	  """
75	  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
76	    user
77	    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
78	    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
79	    |> validate_password(opts)
80	  end
81	
82	  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
83	    changeset
84	    |> validate_required([:password])
85	    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
86	    # Examples of additional password validation:
87	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
88	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
89	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
90	    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
91	  end
92	
93	  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
94	    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
95	    password = get_change(changeset, :password)
96	
97	    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
98	      changeset
99	      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
100	      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
101	      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
102	      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
103	      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
104	      |> delete_change(:password)
105	    else
106	      changeset
107	    end
108	  end
109	
110	  @doc """
111	  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for changing the password.

  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.

  ## Options

    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
    |> validate_password(opts)
  end

  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
    changeset
    |> validate_required([:password])
    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
    # Examples of additional password validation:
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
  end

  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
    password = get_change(changeset, :password)

    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
      changeset
      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
      |> delete_change(:password)
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
  """
  def confirm_changeset(user) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
  end

  @doc """
  Verifies the password.

  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call
  `Bcrypt.no_user_verify/0` to avoid timing attacks.
  """
  def valid_password?(%CleanerCrm.Users.User{hashed_password: hashed_password}, password)
      when is_binary(hashed_password) and byte_size(password) > 0 do
    Bcrypt.verify_pass(password, hashed_password)
  end

  def valid_password?(_, _) do
    Bcrypt.no_user_verify()
    false
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users do
  @moduledoc """
  The Users context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{User, UserToken, UserNotifier}

  ## Database getters

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email("foo@example.com")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email("unknown@example.com")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email(email) when is_binary(email) do
    Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email and password.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "correct_password")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "invalid_password")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email_and_password(email, password)
      when is_binary(email) and is_binary(password) do
    user = Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
    if User.valid_password?(user, password), do: user
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a single user.

  Raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` if the User does not exist.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user!(123)
      %User{}

      iex> get_user!(456)
      ** (Ecto.NoResultsError)

  """

      |> then(&Clients.create_property(scope, &1))

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    cast(plan, attrs, @fields)
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
2	  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes
3	
4	  import Plug.Conn
5	  import Phoenix.Controller
6	
7	  alias CleanerCrm.Users
8	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
9	
10	  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
11	  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
12	  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
13	  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
14	  @remember_me_options [
15	    sign: true,
16	    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
17	    same_site: "Lax"
18	  ]
19	
20	  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
21	  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
22	  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
23	  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
24	  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
25	  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
26	  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
27	  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7
28	
29	  @doc """
30	  Logs the user in.
31	
32	  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
33	  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
34	  """
35	  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
36	    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)
37	
38	    conn
39	    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
40	    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
41	  end
42	
43	  @doc """
44	  Logs the user out.
45	
46	  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
47	  """
48	  def log_out_user(conn) do
49	    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
50	    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)
51	
52	    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
53	      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
54	    end
55	
56	    conn
57	    |> renew_session(nil)
58	    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
59	    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
60	  end
61	
62	  @doc """
63	  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.
64	
65	  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
66	  """
67	  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
68	    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
69	         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
70	      conn
71	      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
72	      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
73	    else
74	      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
75	    end
76	  end
77	
78	  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
79	    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
80	      {token, conn}
81	    else
82	      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])
83	
84	      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
85	        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
86	      else
87	        nil
88	      end
89	    end
90	  end
91	
92	  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
93	  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
94	    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)
95	
96	    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
97	      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
98	    else
99	      conn
100	    end
101	  end
102	
103	  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
104	  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
105	  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
106	  # will soon expire.
107	  #
108	  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
109	  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
110	  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
111	  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
112	    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
113	    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)
114	
115	    conn
116	    |> renew_session(user)
117	    |> put_token_in_session(token)
118	    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
119	  end
120	
121	  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
122	  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
123	  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
124	    conn
125	  end
126	
127	  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
128	  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
129	  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
130	  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
131	  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
132	  #
133	  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
134	  #       delete_csrf_token()
135	  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
136	  #
137	  #       conn
138	  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
139	  #       |> clear_session()
140	  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
141	  #     end
142	  #
143	  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
144	    delete_csrf_token()
145	
146	    conn
147	    |> configure_session(renew: true)
148	    |> clear_session()
149	  end
150	
151	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
152	    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)
153	
154	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
155	    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)
156	
157	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn
158	
159	  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
160	    conn
161	    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
162	    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
163	  end
164	
165	  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
166	    conn
167	    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
168	    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
169	  end
170	
171	  @doc """
172	  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
173	  """
174	  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
175	    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
176	      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
177	    end)
178	  end
179	
180	  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"
181	
182	  @doc """
183	  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.
184	
185	  ## `on_mount` arguments
186	
187	    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
188	      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
189	      there's no user_token or no matching user.
190	
191	    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
192	      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
193	      on user_token.
194	      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.
195	
196	  ## Examples
197	
198	  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
199	  the `current_scope`:
200	
201	      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
202	        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view
203	
204	        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
205	        ...
206	      end
207	
208	  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:
209	
210	      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
211	        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
212	      end
213	  """
214	  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
215	    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
216	  end
217	
218	  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
219	    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)
220	
221	    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
222	      {:cont, socket}
223	    else
224	      socket =
225	        socket
226	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
227	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
228	
229	      {:halt, socket}
230	    end
231	  end
232	
233	  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
234	    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)
235	
236	    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
237	      {:cont, socket}
238	    else
239	      socket =
240	        socket
241	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
242	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
243	
244	      {:halt, socket}
