defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetExportController do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking

  def show(conn, %{"start_date" => start_date, "end_date" => end_date}) do
    period = {Date.from_iso8601!(start_date), Date.from_iso8601!(end_date)}

    case TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(conn.assigns.current_scope, period) do
      {:ok, csv} ->
        conn
        |> put_resp_content_type("text/csv")
        |> put_resp_header(
          "content-disposition",
          ~s(attachment; filename="payroll-#{start_date}-#{end_date}.csv")
        )
        |> send_resp(200, csv)

      {:error, :unresolved_entries} ->
        conn
        |> put_flash(:error, "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting")
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/timesheets")
    end
  end
end

      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index

      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create

  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.EarningsTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  describe "job_cents/2" do
    test "piece-rate pays the flat amount regardless of entries" do
      job = %Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: 8000}

      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, []) == 8000
      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, [resolved_entry(hours: 5)]) == 8000
    end

    test "hourly pays the rate times worked hours" do
      job = %Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: 2500}

      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, [resolved_entry(hours: 2.5)]) == 6250
    end

    test "hourly sums worked time across multiple resolved entries" do
      job = %Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: 2000}

      entries = [resolved_entry(hours: 1), resolved_entry(hours: 2)]
      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, entries) == 6000
    end

    test "hourly is nil with no entries yet" do
      job = %Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: 2500}
      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, []) == nil
    end

    test "hourly is nil while any entry is still open" do
      job = %Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: 2500}
      entries = [resolved_entry(hours: 1), open_entry()]

      assert Earnings.job_cents(job, entries) == nil
    end

    test "nil pay type never defaults to a price" do
      assert Earnings.job_cents(%Job{}, [resolved_entry(hours: 3)]) == nil
    end
  end

  describe "worked_seconds/1 and elapsed_seconds/1" do
    test "worked_seconds is the resolved clock-in to clock-out span" do
      entry = resolved_entry(hours: 2)
      assert Earnings.worked_seconds(entry) == 7200
    end

    test "elapsed_seconds counts from clock-in to now for an open entry" do
      entry = %TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -600, :second)}
      assert_in_delta Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry), 600, 2
    end
  end

  defp resolved_entry(hours: hours) do
    clocked_in_at = ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z]
    clocked_out_at = DateTime.add(clocked_in_at, round(hours * 3600), :second)
    %TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: clocked_in_at, clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}
  end

  defp open_entry, do: %TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z], clocked_out_at: nil}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTrackingTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

    cleaner = user_fixture()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "clock_in/2 and clock_out/2" do
    test "rejects a cleaner who isn't assigned to the job", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      other = user_fixture()
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, other, %{})

      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: other}
      _ = cleaner_scope

      assert {:error, :not_assigned} =
               TimeTracking.clock_in(%{scope | user: user_fixture()}, job)
    end

    test "clocks in and out, recording worked time", %{scope: scope, client: client, cleaner: cleaner} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert entry.clocked_out_at == nil

      assert {:ok, resolved} = TimeTracking.clock_out(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert resolved.clocked_out_at != nil
    end

    test "refuses a second clock-in while already clocked in elsewhere", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job_a = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      job_b = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, _entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job_a)
      assert {:error, {:already_clocked_in, ^job_a}} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job_b)
    end
  end

  describe "pay calculations via list_job_time_summaries/2" do
    test "hourly and piece-rate jobs both contribute to the period total", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      hourly_job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{
          pay_type: :hourly,
          hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
          status: :completed
        })

      TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
        job_id: hourly_job.id,
        clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
        clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:30:00Z]
      })

      period = TimeTracking.pay_period_for(~D[2024-01-08])
      totals = TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period)

      assert totals[cleaner.id] == 6250
    end

    test "an unresolved entry is excluded from the pay total and blocks export", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{status: :scheduled})

      {:ok, entry} =
        TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z]
        })

      period = TimeTracking.pay_period_for(~D[2024-01-08])

      assert TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period)[cleaner.id] == 0
      assert {:error, :unresolved_entries} = TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(scope, period)

      {:ok, _resolved} =
        TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out(scope, entry, %{clock_out_time: "11:00"})

      assert {:ok, csv} = TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(scope, period)
      assert csv =~ cleaner.email
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.AddTimeTrackingPayFields do
  use Ecto.Migration

  # Additive columns only — `jobs` and `accounts` stay owned by
  # Scheduling/Accounts, but a job's pay arrangement and an account's
  # drive-time policy are read and written by TimeTracking (the same
  # relationship `agreed_price_cents` already has with Billing).
  def change do
    alter table(:jobs) do
      add :pay_type, :string
      add :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
      add :piece_rate_cents, :integer
    end

    alter table(:accounts) do
      add :drive_time_policy, :string, null: false, default: "unpaid"
    end
  end
end
---
defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.CreateTimeTrackingTables do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    create table(:time_entries, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :job_id, references(:jobs, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all), null: false
      add :cleaner_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)

      add :clocked_in_at, :utc_datetime_usec, null: false
      add :clocked_out_at, :utc_datetime_usec

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:time_entries, [:account_id])
    create index(:time_entries, [:job_id])
    create index(:time_entries, [:cleaner_id, :clocked_out_at])

    create table(:pay_rates, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :cleaner_id, references(:users, on_delete: :delete_all), null: false

      add :basis, :string, null: false
      add :rate_cents, :integer, null: false

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create unique_index(:pay_rates, [:account_id, :cleaner_id])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.AccountsRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}

  def create_account(attrs) do
    %Account{}
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def get_account(id), do: Repo.get(Account, id)
  def get_account!(id), do: Repo.get!(Account, id)

  def update_account(%Account{} = account, attrs) do
    account
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def delete_account(%Account{} = account), do: Repo.delete(account)

  def create_account_with_owner(attrs, owner_id) do
    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, account} <- create_account(attrs),
           {:ok, _member} <-
             create_member(%{user_id: owner_id, account_id: account.id, role: :owner}) do
        account
      else
        {:error, reason} -> Repo.rollback(reason)
      end
    end)
  end

  def by_slug(slug), do: from(a in Account, where: a.slug == ^slug)
  def with_preloads(preloads), do: from(a in Account, preload: ^preloads)

  defp create_member(attrs) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    clocked_in_at |> DateTime.to_date() |> DateTime.new(time, time_zone)
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: Earnings.job_cents(job, entries),
        unresolved?: Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTrackingTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

    cleaner = user_fixture()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "clock_in/2 and clock_out/2" do
    test "rejects a cleaner who isn't assigned to the job", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: assigned_cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, assigned_cleaner, %{})
      someone_else_scope = %{scope | user: user_fixture()}

      assert {:error, :not_assigned} = TimeTracking.clock_in(someone_else_scope, job)
    end

    test "clocks in and out, recording worked time", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert entry.clocked_out_at == nil

      assert {:ok, resolved} = TimeTracking.clock_out(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert resolved.clocked_out_at != nil
    end

    test "refuses a second clock-in while already clocked in elsewhere", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job_a = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      job_b = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, _entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job_a)
      assert {:error, {:already_clocked_in, ^job_a}} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job_b)
    end
  end

  describe "pay calculations via list_job_time_summaries/2" do
    test "an hourly job's pay accumulates into the cleaner's period total", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      hourly_job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{
          pay_type: :hourly,
          hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
          status: :completed
        })

      TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
        job_id: hourly_job.id,
        clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
        clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:30:00Z]
      })

      period = TimeTracking.pay_period_for(~D[2024-01-08])
      totals = TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period)

      assert totals[cleaner.id] == 6250
    end

    test "an unresolved entry is excluded from the pay total and blocks export", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{status: :scheduled})

      {:ok, entry} =
        TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z]
        })

      period = TimeTracking.pay_period_for(~D[2024-01-08])

      assert TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period)[cleaner.id] == 0
      assert {:error, :unresolved_entries} = TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(scope, period)

        TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out(scope, entry, %{clock_out_time: "11:00"})

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

    mix spex
    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
    mix spex --verbose
    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
    mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
    mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
    mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
    mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

## Configuration

You can configure spex behavior in your config files:

    config :sexy_spex,
      manual_mode: false,
      step_delay: 0

Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all

input.new_string:
# Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    clocked_in_at |> DateTime.to_date() |> DateTime.new(time, time_zone)
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
        # — an open entry is the expected cause, but a job missing its
        # pay type entirely (`cents` still `nil` once every entry is
        # closed) must block the same way, not silently price at $0.
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents)
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

Everything still compiles cleanly and all 13 TimeTracking tests pass after the Scheduling agent's concurrent update to `job.ex` — my additions were compatible and left intact. The team-lead has already been sent the final report.

To summarize what was delivered:

**TimeTracking slice implementation** (`/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm`):
- Context: `lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking.ex` — clock in/out, time entry CRUD, pay-period calculations, CSV export, drive-time policy, pay rates
- Schemas: `lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking/{time_entry,pay_rate}.ex`
- Pure calculation modules: `lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking/{earnings,payroll_export}.ex`

I also fixed a pre-existing gap in the shared fixtures file where `job_fixture` didn't supply required `scheduled_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` defaults, which was breaking job creation for every story, not just this one.

**Spex results:** Story 838 passes 4/8 (the four TimesheetLive-driven criteria: hourly pay, piece-rate pay, running pay-period total, CSV export); the other 4 stay red because they drive `/field/jobs/:id`, which is `FieldLive.Job` — not yet built by another agent.   use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

    cleaner = user_fixture()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

content.text:
I've fixed the reported `PayrollExport` bug and confirmed the full suite is clean. Summary of what happened:

**Root cause:** `list_job_time_summaries/2` determined whether a job was "unresolved" purely from `is_nil(cents)`. That missed a piece-rate job with an open (not-yet-clocked-out) time entry — piece rate always computes its flat cents regardless of entry state, so such a job never got flagged unresolved and slipped through to `PayrollExport.cleaner_row/1`, which then called `Earnings.worked_seconds/1` on the still-open entry and crashed (matching the `nil + 0` arithmetic error reported).

**Fix:** in `lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking.ex`, `unresolved?` is now `is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))` — covering both "no computable pay type" and "still has an open entry," so `export_pay_period_csv/2` blocks correctly before ever reaching CSV building. Added a regression test in `test/cleaner_crm/time_tracking_test.exs` for exactly this scenario.

**Verified:** `mix test` now passes 146/146 (was already 145/145 before this addition — the new regression test brings it to 146), `mix format --check-formatted` is clean, and `mix compile` has no errors. Regarding the fixtures scope note — no action was needed on my part since I was already reusing the existing `scoped_to_account` helper rather than writing my own version.

end

  def handle_info(:checklist_changed, socket), do: {:noreply, load_checklist(socket)}

  def handle_info(:tick, socket) do
    if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000)
    {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)}
  end

  defp maybe_schedule_tick(socket) do
    if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000)
    socket
  end

  defp assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job), do: job.cleaner_id == scope.user.id

  defp office_staff?(%{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
  end

  defp office_staff?(_scope), do: false

  # Every job gets a checklist to complete through, even a trivially
  # empty one for a job nothing ever assigned a template to — lazily
  # instantiated here so `ChecklistComponent`'s completion flow (and
  # the invoice it triggers) is the one path every job completes
  # through, rather than a second one this view would otherwise need
  # for the no-checklist case.
  defp load_checklist(socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
    job = socket.assigns.job

    checklist =
      case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do
        nil ->
          {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])
          checklist

        checklist ->
          checklist
      end

    assign(socket, :checklist, checklist)
  end

  defp load_time_state(socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
    job = socket.assigns.job
    entries = TimeTracking.list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job)
    last_resolved = entries |> Enum.filter(&TimeEntry.resolved?/1) |> List.last()

    socket
    |> assign(:open_entry, TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job))
    |> assign(:elapsed_seconds, TimeTracking.elapsed_seconds(scope, job))
    |> assign(:last_worked_seconds, last_resolved && worked_seconds(last_resolved))
    |> assign(:earnings_cents, TimeTracking.job_earnings_cents(scope, job))
  end

  # `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` is an internal submodule not
  # exported by its boundary — this mirrors its own `worked_seconds/1`
  # for the one thing this view needs from it (a resolved entry's
  # clocked duration), without reaching across the boundary.
  defp worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at}),
    do: DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)

  defp client_name(%{client: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name
  defp client_name(%{property: %{client: %{name: name}}}) when is_binary(name), do: name
  defp client_name(_job), do: "Job"

  defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-H:%M")

  defp format_duration(nil), do: "0m"

  defp format_duration(seconds) do
    hours = div(seconds, 3600)
    minutes = div(rem(seconds, 3600), 60)
    "#{hours}h #{minutes}m"
  end
end

content.text:
Fixed and reported. Summary of this round:

**Bug fixed:** The `KeyError: key :value not found` crash in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex` was caused by `CoreComponents.input`'s `:value` attribute having no default — my resolve-clock-out time input omitted it, and the catch-all render clause tried to reference `@value` directly. Added `value=""` to fix it.

**Result:** Story 838 is now 7/8 passing (up from 4/8 last round). The one remaining failure, criterion 7137, asserts that after a cleaner clocks in, their own `FieldLive.Job` page (`lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex`) shows "Missing clock-out" text — that file is off-limits to me per the team lead's instructions, and currently has no such rendering at all (it only shows "Clocked in" + elapsed time). I flagged this precisely rather than touching it.

**Bonus fix within scope:** I noticed `FieldLive.Job` had to hand-duplicate `Earnings.worked_seconds/1` locally with a comment explaining it couldn't reach across the boundary — because I'd never exported `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings`. Added that export to `lib/cleaner_crm.ex` so it's available directly.

Full suite: `mix test` is 146/146 passing, `mix compile` and `mix format --check-formatted` are both clean.
